title: Pic of a proper curve: divisibility, n-torsion, cokernel
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve of
genus $g$ over algebraically closed $k$, and let $n$ be prime
to $\operatorname{char}k$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g},
\qquad
\operatorname{coker}\bigl(n:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\bigr)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z,
$$

and $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ is $n$-divisible.

proof.text: The proper curve $C$ has dimension one by [def-sc-curves], so it is projective by [lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective]. By [lem-sc-smooth-regular], all its local rings are domains. Hence distinct irreducible components cannot meet. The field spectrum is Noetherian, so finite type of $C$ over $k$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] make $C$ Noetherian. Its finitely many irreducible components are then also open; connectedness leaves exactly one. Thus $C$ is integral and is a curve in the sense of [def-pc-curve], projective and smooth in the sense of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. As $C$ is nonempty and smooth over the separably closed field $k$, [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] gives $P\in C(k)$; [prop-pc-xk-integral] applied to $(C,P)$ now makes $C$ geometrically integral. Therefore [thm-sc-jacobian-representability] applies and identifies $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of [def-sc-pic0] with $J_C(k)$ for an abelian variety $J_C$ of dimension $g$: the genus in its statement agrees with [def-sc-genus] by [lem-pc-genus-agrees-sc].

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence; projectivity input Stacks Project Varieties Lemma 0A26 (varieties-lemma-dim-1-proper-projective)

proof.text: The degree sequence splits by [lem-sc-pic-proper-decomposition]: $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$, where the second factor is the kernel of degree [def-sc-pic0]. By the group identification in step 1, clause (d) of [thm-av-final] makes $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ $n$-divisible. Here $n\geq1$ is understood in the source's phrase 'n prime to the characteristic'; the case $n=1$ is trivial.

By [def-sc-mult-n], $J_C(k)[n]$ is the group of $k$-points of $J_C[n]$. Clause (c) of [thm-av-final], applied with $\dim J_C=g$ from step 1 and $n$ prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, gives $J_C(k)[n]\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$. Under the decomposition in step 2, multiplication by $n$ is componentwise. Since $\mathbf Z[n]=0$ for $n\geq1$, $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)[n]\cong J_C(k)[n]$, proving the torsion clause.

source.place: ## Proof, sentence beginning 'The group J_C(k)' and first displayed conclusion

proof.text: Again use $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ from [lem-sc-pic-proper-decomposition]. Multiplication by $n$ has image $n\mathbf Z\oplus n\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$; step 2 gives $n\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$. Its cokernel is therefore $(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)\oplus0\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, including when $n=1$.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_proper_ntorsion {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsProper f] (n : ℕ) (_hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) : Nonempty ((powMonoidHom n : C.Pic →* C.Pic).ker ≃* Multiplicative (Fin (2 * f.genus) → ZMod n)) ∧ Nonempty (C.Pic ⧸ (powMonoidHom n : C.Pic →* C.Pic).range ≃* Multiplicative (ZMod n)) ∧ (∀ L : C.Pic, L ∈ f.picZero → ∃ M : C.Pic, M ∈ f.picZero ∧ M ^ n = L)
